title: Statistics for Life Sciences I
description: Descriptive statistics; probability; random variables and probability distributions; expectation; binomial, Poisson, and normal distributions; random sampling and sampling distributions; point and interval estimation; classical hypothesis testing and significance testing. Statistical examples and applications from life sciences are emphasized.
notes: Credit will be granted for only one of STAT 255, STAT 252.
Not open to students registered in or with credit in one of STAT 254, STAT 250, STAT 260.
See "Credit Limit - Beginning Level Statistics Courses".

Intended primarily for students in Biology, Environmental Studies combined with a Science discipline, Kinesiology, Molecular Life Sciences, and Combined Computer Science and Health Information Science.

prerequisites.text: 1.5 units of MATH course numbered 100 or higher.
